items.title: Neal Caine interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, September 26, 2019
items.q: I was doing my kind of Jimmy, you know my thing.

ctx.x: If an interviewer, you know, got an interview with him and opened the first thing they said was, “Mr. Jones tell us about John Coltrane.” How would be react to that?

Well it would probably depend on his mood at that particular moment, but he would say he was an angel. He loved John Coltrane. He was a genius and an angel. I mean he used to talk about, I mean I was lucky enough to spend some time with him and he loved — he used to talk about the Basie band, Duke’s band, and then like you know one time I remember we were playing at the New Morning. And it would be like an open bass solo. And I was doing my kind of Jimmy, you know my thing. And my end pin broke. And maybe I…

I think I know what you’re saying, because I’ve been fortunate to interview a lot of folks from that generation, and they’re serious. And they’re always dressed up and they’re always a take care of the bandstand type attitude. Why would that change? © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-
